summary.text:
Compiled on first attempt. Let me verify the behavior against the tests mentally.

Test 1 step 0: Start=true, RetractDone=false → stays IDLE, Busy false, Done false. ✓
Step 1: Start=true, RetractDone=true → EXTEND, Extend true, Busy true. ✓
Step 2: no feedback → stays EXTEND, Extend true. ✓
Step 3: ExtendDone → CLAMP, Clamp true. ✓
Step 4: ClampDone → RELEASE. But wait, in step 4 inputs: ExtendDone=false, ClampDone=true. Pre-state CLAMP → transition to RELEASE, Release true, Clamp false. ✓
Step 5: ReleaseDone → RETRACT ✓
Step 6: RetractDone → DONE, Busy false, Done true ✓
Step 7: Start true in DONE → ignored, Done true ✓
Step 8: Reset → IDLE ✓

Test 2: all feedbacks true, Start true → IDLE with RetractDone true → EXTEND. Extend true only. ✓ Then next scan pre-state EXTEND, ExtendDone true → CLAMP ✓. Then CLAMP, ClampDone → RELEASE ✓. Then Stop → IDLE all clear ✓. Then Reset ✓.

P2: Stop/Reset produces IDLE with all outputs false ✓. P8: qDone normal → Done ✓.

Note for P9: qExtend & !ExtendDone → Extend, and ExtendDone → Clamp (so Extend false). That's consistent with the LTL? P9 only asserts Extend when not done. Fine.

One thing: the "first" proposition mentions true on first invocation — not required.

Done.

output.arguments:
{"answer": "Implemented FB_Task (SELF011) in CODESYS 3.5 ST with a six-state machine (E_TaskState DUT: IDLE, EXTEND, CLAMP, RELEASE, RETRACT, DONE) and compiled successfully on the first attempt (0 errors, 0 warnings, backend CODESYS, status PASS).

Behavior:
- Stop or Reset has top priority: forces IDLE and clears every command/output in the same scan.
- Exactly one transition per scan, evaluated from the retained pre-state in a CASE, so simultaneous TRUE handshakes cannot skip states.
- IDLE accepts Start only when RetractDone (home) is TRUE, then goes to EXTEND.
- EXTEND --ExtendDone--> CLAMP --ClampDone--> RELEASE --ReleaseDone--> RETRACT --RetractDone--> DONE.
- DONE holds (Done = TRUE) until Stop/Reset; Start during Busy or DONE is ignored.
- Extend/Clamp/Release/Retract are TRUE only in their corresponding post-transition state; Busy is TRUE in those four action states; Done only in DONE (so at most one action is ever TRUE).

Traces from the specification were checked against the code logic manually; no PLC hardware/functional tests were executed."}
